question.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨t,\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ as a function of $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-{e}^{-t})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{-2t}+1} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}{{e}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,{e}^{-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,{e}^{-t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{-t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & ={e}^{-t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖={e}^{-t}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-t}}{{(\frac{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}{{e}^{t}})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-t}}{(\frac{\sqrt{{({e}^{2t}+1)}^{3}}}{{e}^{3t}})} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{{({e}^{2t}+1)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
